# models.dev

The price and capability snapshot bundled at `src/data/model-metadata.json`,
generated by `scripts/build-model-metadata.mjs` (`pnpm models:build`).

Upstream: <https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev>, MIT licensed — the full
text is in `LICENSE` beside this file, and it is shipped in every desktop
distribution as `licenses/models-dev/LICENSE` (`electron-builder.yml`).

The API served at <https://models.dev/api.json> is fetched once, by hand, when
the snapshot is refreshed. **The app never calls it.** The snapshot is compiled
into the renderer bundle by Vite, so there is no runtime request, no cache, and
no "last refreshed N days ago" state in front of a user — Sean's decision,
2026-09-18.

## Taken

Per model, seven fields, all from the upstream record:

| snapshot field     | upstream field                  |
|--------------------|---------------------------------|
| `name`             | `name`                          |
| `inputPerMillion`  | `cost.input`                    |
| `outputPerMillion` | `cost.output`                   |
| `contextWindow`    | `limit.context`                 |
| `vision`           | `"image" in modalities.input`   |
| `tools`            | `tool_call`                     |
| `reasoning`        | `reasoning`                     |

Plus each kept provider's `name`.

## Not taken

Everything else upstream carries: `description`, `family`, `knowledge`,
`release_date`, `last_updated`, `open_weights`, `temperature`,
`structured_output`, `reasoning_options`, `limit.output`, `cost.cache_read`,
`cost.cache_write`, `modalities.output`, and every provider-level field
(`env`, `npm`, `api`, `doc`). None of it reaches the picker.

**No provider is dropped.** All 221 are kept — 7,842 models, 1.6 MB on disk,
1.1 MB as Vite inlines it, 122 KB gzipped inside the asar.

This began as a 13-provider allow-list of what Murage can reach, which cut the
file to 133 KB. It was the wrong trade and was reverted (Sean, 2026-09-18): an
`openai-compat` connection can point at any of these gateways, OpenRouter alone
re-exposes most of the field, and a user seeing "Price unavailable" on a model
we could have priced is a worse outcome than a megabyte of JSON. Keeping
everything also *reduced* refusals rather than raising them, because
`VENDOR_PROVIDERS` in `src/lib/model-metadata.ts` settles a reseller
disagreement on the vendor's own published rate.

`fluxrouter.ai` is not in models.dev and is not wanted there: `flux-auto` and
its sibling tiers are routes over several models, so they have no single price.
`src/lib/model-metadata.ts` refuses to price them rather than inventing a band.
Flux's `flux-pinned-<model>` rows DO name a concrete model and are matched on
the remainder, which is what gives Flux Router's pinned catalogue real bands.

## Freshness

The snapshot records its own `source.fetchedAt` and the upstream `ETag`, and
carries a SHA-256 `digest` of its provider tree. `pnpm models:check` — wired
into `pnpm test` and into CI — re-renders the committed file from itself and
compares both the bytes and the digest, so a stale or hand-edited snapshot
fails the gate. That check never touches the network; only `pnpm models:build`
does.
